sections.title: The Inheritance of the Half-Tribe of Manasseh
observations: This section discusses the allocation of land to the half-tribe of Manasseh, which was divided between the eastern and western sides of the Jordan River. The eastern side was already settled, while the western side was still being distributed.

The request of the daughters of Zelophehad for their inheritance is significant as it highlights the importance of women in the inheritance laws of Israel. This reflects God's justice and provision for all His people.

sections.title: The Challenge of the Remaining Land
observations: The descendants of Joseph, which includes both Ephraim and Manasseh, express their concern about the size of their inheritance. They feel that their portion is too small given their population and the blessings they have received from God.
Joshua encourages them to take possession of the hill country and to clear the land of the Canaanites, emphasizing the need for action and faith in God's promises.

sections.title: The Canaanites and Their Defeat
observations: The chapter concludes with a discussion about the Canaanites who remain in the land. Despite their strength and chariots, Joshua reassures the people that they can drive them out with God's help.
This serves as a reminder that faith in God is essential for overcoming obstacles, no matter how formidable they may seem.

importantVerses.commentary: The daughters of Zelophehad's request for their inheritance demonstrates the inclusivity of God's promises and the importance of justice in the distribution of land.
Joshua's encouragement to the descendants of Joseph to take the hill country illustrates the necessity of faith and action in claiming God's promises.

questions: What does the request of the daughters of Zelophehad teach us about God's justice and provision for all His people?
How can we apply Joshua's encouragement to take action in our own lives when facing challenges?
What does this chapter reveal about the importance of faith in overcoming obstacles?
